title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ནེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 181)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio from the Pramāṇa section: a word-by-word commentary on a pramāṇa root verse ("སྔར་གྱི་བློ་ནི་ནུས་ཟད་ན།") about cognition, ālayavijñāna and pravṛttivijñāna. It belongs on this shelf.
structure_note: The scan's own margin number reads 433 and the record's page_number is 432. The text matches the image, so this is a sequence-offset label, not a wrong leaf.

tr_errors_A.english: The previous cognition perishes after producing its own subsequent cognition. Regarding the objection, "Is it not the case that cognition of an object arises merely from the proximity..."
tr_errors_A.problem: The first clause (ཡིན་ལ) belongs inside the opponent's statement that ends at ཞེས་ཟེར་བ. A gives it in the author's voice as a standalone claim, so the opponent's premise is attributed to the commentator.

tr_errors_A.english: the text removes the problem of exhaustion ... by stating, "if to me,"
tr_errors_A.problem: The source refutes a shift of cognition that is claimed to come from fatigue (the opponent's position). A says instead that the text 'removes the problem of exhaustion', which garbles the line of argument.

tr_errors_A.english: if the vision of previous moments of intellect is impaired
tr_errors_A.problem: Misparse: the source says the capacity declines through the seeing done by each earlier cognition. A makes the 'vision' the thing that is impaired.
The connective དེ་ཡང and the emphatic ཡང ('also') are dropped.
The note says 'original' for a Sanskrit term that is not on this Tibetan page. It is a back-reconstruction presented as if it were the source.

tr_errors_B.english: what cannot arise from incapacity does not arise
tr_errors_B.problem: The final སྐྱེ་བ ('arises') is turned into 'does not arise', which produces a tautology. The Tibetan is itself awkward here.

tr_errors_B.english: the refutation based on cognitive fatigue is introduced
tr_errors_B.problem: Slightly loose: it is a refutation of shift-from-fatigue, not a refutation 'based on' fatigue.

pages.prefer_reason: B keeps the opponent's whole objection in the opponent's voice and parses the 'declines through the earlier cognitions' clause correctly. A misattributes the opponent's premise and garbles the fatigue refutation.

book_verdict: A clean Derge Pramāṇa commentary folio with an accurate transcription. Translation B is the better of the two; A has moderate errors of speaker attribution and argument structure, but neither has a serious error.
